text:
Done.

## What changed

**`src/logger.h`** — added `LOG_WARNING()`, declared `inline auto LOG_WARNING() -> std::ostream &` next to `LOG_VERBOSE`. It always writes `"warning: "` to `std::cerr` and returns `std::cerr`, independent of `--verbose` or any option. Added `<iostream> // std::cerr` to the existing include block.

**Warning sites converted to `LOG_WARNING() << <message>`:**
- `src/command_lint.cc` — unknown-rule warning (was `LOG_VERBOSE`-gated)
- `src/command_validate.cc` — invalid pre-compiled template warning, and the empty-JSONL warning (was `LOG_VERBOSE`-gated), so both now always print
- `src/resolver.h` — multi-line "No schema resources…" warning merged into one `LOG_WARNING()` chain (one prefix, continuation lines follow it)
- `src/command_bundle.cc` — six-line `--without-id` warning merged into one `LOG_WARNING()` chain; added `#include "logger.h"`

**`test/validate/pass_jsonl_empty.sh`** — expected stderr now includes `warning: The JSONL file is empty`, since that warning is no longer suppressed by non-verbose (the file is already registered in `test/CMakeLists.txt`).

No source hand-spells `warning: ` anymore; the only occurrence in `src/` is inside `LOG_WARNING()`.

## Evidence

- `make configure compile` → exit 0 (clang-format and shellcheck targets clean, binary built/installed/packaged).
- `ctest --test-dir build -R 'pass_jsonl_empty' --output-on-failure` → 2/2 passed.
- Full `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --parallel 4` → 301/301 passed.
